narrative: 移轴中的“倾斜”（Tilt）不是一个虚化贴纸。沙姆定律（Scheimpflug relation）让世界的一个切片沿着一个不再与传感器平行的平面变得清晰：一条布满赛艇手的河道、一群人、一整桌突然看起来像玩具的人。
移轴中的“平移”（Shift）是另一项任务：它平移画面，让垂直线条保持平行，或者在不转动摄影机的情况下“绕过”一个转角去看东西。如果你只是想让一张脸从墙面上孤立出来，这不是合适的工具。
那应该用普通焦平面上的浅焦（Shallow Focus）。如果这个微缩模型效果没有一个高机位视角，也没有一条前后一致的对焦带，这也不是合适的工具。
一条无视透视关系的水平虚化条纹，只是后期做出来的假效果，而不是这套光学系统本身。
how: 让镜头倾斜，使焦平面以一条细带或楔形的方式穿过主体。一个高机位角度有助于营造微缩模型的观感，因为我们是俯视着这些“模型”的。
让虚化程度与景深相匹配；随着透视关系的变化，这条清晰带应该跟随那个平面移动，而不是一条平面化的2D条纹。如果需要校正建筑物汇聚变形，就独立使用平移功能。
提示词：A real-scale city or citadel with [Subject] human-sized. A thin band of focus across the subject, foreground and far ground softly blurred, no hard seam across the frame.
when: 用它把一座城市变成一个模型，或者沿着一个倾斜的平面切出一条穿过人群的清晰带。不要把它当作浅焦人像的同义词，也不要在一张平面化的图像上直接铺一条虚化条。
vs: 浅焦让焦平面与传感器保持平行，靠距离来实现孤立感；移轴中的“倾斜”则旋转了那个焦平面。
微距是近距离尺度，而不是一座城市的立体模型；鸟瞰（Bird's-Eye View）可以提供微缩模型效果常常需要的高机位视角，但没有倾斜焦平面的鸟瞰，只是一张地图而已。
examples_film: 《社交网络》（The Social Network）里的亨利划船比赛段落，通过一条细窄、高机位的立体模型式对焦，让真实尺度的动作呈现出微缩模型般的观感。其他影片中的“微缩城市”处理也遵循着同样的语法：高机位视角、浅窄的清晰带、看起来像玩具般的运动。
借鉴的是这个焦平面本身，而不是照搬那场比赛的某一张画面。
mistakes: 最常被搞混的近邻是脸部的浅焦，或者一个后期加了2D虚化条纹的伪微缩模型效果。破绽是一张背景奶油般化开的人像，或者一道无视建筑物景深关系的接缝。
解决办法：高机位视角、真人尺度的人物、把焦点当作一个穿过场景的平面来处理，让虚化跟随景深变化。

faq.a: “倾斜”旋转焦平面相对于传感器的角度；“平移”则滑动镜头，在不倾斜摄影机的情况下改变透视关系。两者结合起来，既可以孤立出一条清晰带，也可以让真实场景看起来像模型。
浅焦让焦平面与传感器保持平行，靠距离产生虚化衰减；移轴则可以让一道楔形或带状的清晰区域穿过整个场景，包括对一座城市的高机位立体模型式取景。区别就在于虚化的形状。
用它在人群中切出一条清晰带，或者把真实尺度的动作变成一个模型。如果只是需要一支快速的85mm来拍普通人像，就跳过它。

faq.q: How do I prompt tilt-shift for AI image or video?
faq.a: 写明主体是真人尺度、身处一座真实的城市里，带有一条细窄的清晰带，没有生硬的接缝。为了立体模型效果，加上一个高机位视角。禁止平面化的虚化条纹和普通人像式的散景。

narrative: Tilt is not a blur sticker. The Scheimpflug relation puts a slice of the world in focus along a plane that is no longer parallel to the sensor: a street of rowers, a crowd, a tabletop of people who suddenly read as toys.
Shift is a different job: it slides the image to keep verticals parallel or to look around a corner without rotating the camera. It is the wrong tool when you only wanted a face isolated from a wall.
That is Shallow Focus on a normal plane. It is also the wrong tool if the miniature effect has no high viewpoint and no consistent focus band.
A horizontal blur strip that ignores perspective is a post fake, not this optic.
how: Tilt the lens so the focus plane cuts through the subject as a thin band or a wedge. A high angle helps the diorama reading because we look down on models.
Match blur to depth; as perspective changes, the band should follow the plane, not a 2D stripe. Shift independently if you need to correct converging buildings.
Prompt: A real-scale city or citadel with [Subject] human-sized. A thin band of focus across the subject, foreground and far ground softly blurred, no hard seam across the frame.
when: Use it to make a city a model, or to slice focus through a crowd on a tilted plane. Do not use it as a synonym for shallow portrait focus, and do not lay a blur bar across a flat image.
vs: Shallow Focus keeps the focus plane parallel to the sensor and isolates by distance. Tilt rotates that plane.
Macro is close-up scale, not a diorama of a city. Bird's-Eye View can supply the high viewpoint the miniature reading often needs, but a bird's-eye without a tilted focus plane is just a map.
examples_film: The Social Network 's Henley rowing sequence gives real-scale action a miniature-like appearance through a thin, high, diorama focus. Miniature-city treatments in other films follow the same grammar: high view, shallow band, motion that reads like a toy.
Borrow the plane, not a still of the race.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is Shallow Focus on a face, or a post miniature with a 2D blur strip. The tell is a portrait with creamy background, or a seam that ignores buildings' depth.
Fix: high view, human-sized figures, focus as a plane through the scene, blur that follows depth.

faq.a: Tilt rotates the plane of focus relative to the sensor. Shift slides the lens to change perspective without tilting the camera. Together they can isolate a band of sharpness or make real scenes read as models.

Shallow focus keeps the focus plane parallel to the sensor and falls off with distance. Tilt-shift can put a wedge or band of focus through a scene, including a high diorama view of a city. Blur shape is the difference.
Use it to slice focus through a crowd or to turn real-scale action into a model. Skip it for ordinary portraits that only need a fast 85mm.

faq.q: How do I prompt tilt-shift for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write that the subject is human-sized in a real city, with a thin band of focus and no hard seam. Add a high viewpoint for the diorama. Forbid a flat blur stripe and ordinary portrait bokeh.
